message.content:
Sure! To post a comment on an IP address in VirusTotal’s database you’ll need to send a **POST** request to the `/ip_addresses/{resource}/comments` endpoint. Below is a quick guide along with a ready‑to‑use `curl` command so you can run it yourself.

---

### What You Need  
| Item | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **API Key** | Your personal VirusTotal API key (`ABC321`). Keep it secret – don’t share it publicly. |
| **IP Address** | The target IP you’re commenting on (`192.168.1.1`). |
| **Comment JSON** | `{ "type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"} }`. |

> ⚠️ *Make sure your account has permission to write comments.* Some free accounts may only allow read access.

---

### Step‑by‑Step Instructions  

#### 1️⃣ Build the URL  
```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments
```

#### 2️⃣ Set Headers  
* `x-apikey`: Your API key  
* `Content-Type`: `application/json`

#### 3️⃣ Prepare Payload  
```json
{
  "type": "comment",
  "attributes": {
    "text": "Confirmed #malware"
  }
}
```

#### 4️⃣ Send Request  
Below is a sample `curl` command:

```bash
curl -X POST \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/192.168.1.1/comments \
     -H "x-apikey: ABC321" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"type":"comment","attributes":{"text":"Confirmed #malware"}}'
```

If everything goes well, you’ll receive a response similar to:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "<unique-comment-id>",
    "type": "comment",
    "links": { ... },
    "attributes": {
      "date_added": <timestamp>,
      "text": "Confirmed #malware",
      ...
    }
  }
}
```

That confirms the comment was added successfully!

---

### Quick Troubleshooting Tips  

| Issue | Likely Cause | Fix |
|-------|--------------|-----|
| **401 Unauthorized** | Wrong/missing API key | Double‑check the key value and ensure there are no leading/trailing spaces. |
| **403 Forbidden** | Account doesn’t support writing comments | Upgrade plan or contact VirusTotal support. |
| **400 Bad Request** | Malformed payload | Validate JSON structure against the schema above. |
| **429 Too Many Requests** | Rate limit exceeded | Wait a few minutes before retrying. |

---

Feel free to replace the placeholder values (`ABC321`, `192.168.1.1`) with your own data when running the command. If you’d rather use another programming language (Python, JavaScript, etc.), let me know—I can show you a short script too!
